# Norns

> Durable agent runtime. Open source, MIT. The orchestrator holds an append-only event log and dispatches one step at a time; workers in your infrastructure make the LLM calls, run the tools, and hold the API keys. A run outlives any worker, deploy, or orchestrator restart.

Norns is written in Elixir on the BEAM, with PostgreSQL for all persistent state. The orchestrator is a state machine: it never calls a model and never runs a tool. Workers connect over WebSocket, register capabilities (`llm`, `tools`) and the tools they serve, and receive task pushes in a provider-neutral format. Message content is opaque to the core; it routes on roles, tool names, ids and steps.

Every LLM request and response, tool call and result, checkpoint, retry, human question and answer, and sub-agent launch is a versioned, validated event in the log. Run state is rebuilt from the log, not from a process. When a worker disconnects, the tasks it held are re-dispatched with the same task id and idempotency key; with no worker available they queue and flush on the next registration. The delivery guarantee is at-least-once with duplicate suppression: a worker that already ran a side-effecting call reports `tool_duplicate` instead of running it again. Exactly-once requires a destination that dedupes on the key.

Agent states: idle, awaiting_llm, awaiting_tools, waiting (on a human). A run parked on `ask_human` stays parked indefinitely and re-parks on the same question after a restart. Built-in tools intercepted by the orchestrator: `wait`, `ask_human`, `launch_agent`, `list_agents`. Sub-agent launches are authorized server-side by allowlist and depth.

Run API: `GET /runs/:id/events` (full log), `GET /runs/:id/summary` (fixed-size account with signals such as loop, retry_storm, unknown_tool), `POST /runs/:id/fork` (new run from any step, optionally with a different model or system prompt), `POST /runs/:id/retry`, `POST /runs/:id/reply`. Run webhooks deliver a signed POST when a run parks, completes, or fails. Cron triggers start runs on a schedule. Serverless workers declare their tools and a wake URL and are started on demand.

Transient failures retry with exponential backoff, three attempts; rate limits get ten. Token usage and serving model are recorded per call; cost is priced at read time.

Version v0.7. The reference application, Mimir (a Slack knowledge bot), has run on the hosted instance since 2026-04-15. Supported deployment is a single node; multi-node is on the roadmap.

## Project

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/nornscode/norns): Elixir orchestrator source
- [README](https://github.com/nornscode/norns#readme): Quickstart
- [Architecture](https://github.com/nornscode/norns/blob/main/docs/architecture.md): Orchestrator/worker split, worker protocol, event schema, agent states
- [Decision log](https://github.com/nornscode/norns/blob/main/docs/decision-log.md): What is built and why, with dates
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/nornscode/norns/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md): Sequencing and what is not being built
- [OpenAPI spec](https://github.com/nornscode/norns/blob/main/openapi.yaml): HTTP API surface

## SDKs

- [Python SDK](https://github.com/nornscode/norns-sdk-python): Worker and client library, `pip install norns-sdk`
- [Elixir SDK](https://github.com/nornscode/norns-sdk-elixir): Worker and client library, `{:norns_sdk, "~> 0.1"}`

## Tooling

- [nornsctl](https://github.com/nornscode/nornsctl): CLI for running a local orchestrator, scaffolding agent projects, and inspecting agents, runs and event logs

## Examples

- [Hello agent](https://github.com/nornscode/norns-hello-agent): Minimal worker
- [Mimir](https://github.com/nornscode/norns-mimir-agent): Slack knowledge bot, the reference application
- [Sleipnir](https://github.com/nornscode/sleipnir): Coding agent that other agents hand work to

## Install

```
brew install nornscode/tap/nornsctl
nornsctl dev
nornsctl new my-agent && cd my-agent
uv sync && uv run my-agent-worker
```
